scope: Selected ingesthree DESIGN compared with its committed synchronous local core. All design=proposed, including implemented ingesthree local graphs. Current ingest-v2 and common runtime are audited separately.
counting_rule: Count graph-local states excluding shared_states. Count distinct (from,to) edges with from != to; alternative triggers and unchanged-state retries do not add edges. Shared runtime counted once per design, actor framework once for current only. No global products or execution counts.
exclusions: All working-tree/index changes are excluded, especially new async_ingester.rs and async_tests.rs and updated local core/docs. Sources refer to committed HEAD, not live line numbering.

Common runtime ready/running scheduling, generic task failure/cancellation and OS blocking are provided by another auditor. No common runtime graph is recreated. Only role-qualified external dependency entry/wakeup edges appear here.

Synchronous local core has no async queue, task spawn, channel, timer, CPU permit, validation worker or internal request waiter at this HEAD. Its blocking filesystem calls use shared OS/runtime mechanics, not invented asynchronous per-function states.

Router selection, request admission/cancellation, validation, compatibility header and automatic rotation are selected outer-path requirements but unimplemented here. This delegated ledger covers local core, handoff, assignment/attempt, publication and cleanup. No production ingesthree HTTP acknowledgment or capacity reservation protocol is asserted.

Logical byte-budget rejection is a guard in local append, not a wait-for-space queue. Core retains finished-file bytes and has no deletion or budget-decrement API. Exact admission budget/reserve dimensions belong to unimplemented outer intake.
No global configurations, bounded BFS, function-entry phases, per-document multiplicity, attempt multiplicity, worker-count expansion or unsupported difficulty percentage.

Intrinsic Tantivy/merge, S3 service, metastore database transaction internals, OS internals and external-source checkpoint protocols are excluded symmetrically. NewSplits notification is selected but its new-path delivery/recovery mechanics are unspecified.

Assignment response reconciliation, handoff identity/content validation, publication response reconciliation, output-ID isolation and concrete cleanup discovery/progress are unresolved. Semantic requirements are labeled specification/proposal rather than implementation.

Unregistered input objects require reconciliation with upload/register work before deletion. No concrete orphan-input collector or safe-abandonment protocol is selected, so no guessed orphan states or age-based safety rule are counted.

CPU offload/queued work, input streaming versus buffering, index setup RPCs, admission permits, upload semaphore, child-task lifetime, retry timers and notification backpressure are not selected ingesthree execution details.

Index deletion, permanently unprocessable input, Force/WaitFor, host-crash/fsync durability and storage replacement remain unresolved or outside contract. Generic error outcomes do not imply selected policies for them.
No tests or failure injection were run. Existing committed tests were inspected as source evidence only. This is a static audit inventory, not proof of exhaustive state coverage.

edges: open fails before lock acquisition, including immediate try_lock contention
all surviving files recovered and accounting reconstructed
startup scan/repair fails or process exits, releasing lock
pre-mutation request rejection leaves owner usable
appending or finishing a file returns error after mutation guard is set
appending or finishing a file rejected until reopen
drop/process exit or consuming finish, successful or failed
drop/process exit or rejected consuming finish releases owner
graphs.notes: Owner is directory-wide, including every index. Recovery holds the lock but enables no intake. failed=true temporarily during a successful synchronous mutation is not a separate state. A failed attempt to finish a file has removed its active entry and requires reopen. finish consumes self even on error. No_owner means this ownership instance is absent, not proof that no other process owns the directory. Lock survives writer destruction. Successful ordinary operations leave usability unchanged and are represented in file/ack dimensions rather than duplicated here.

edges: first accepted append for an index creates fresh ULID path
header written and flushed, then rename succeeds
append reuses active file for same full IndexUid
manually finishing one or all files flushes and renames
startup preserves complete documents, repairs allowed tail if needed, then renames under same ID
startup scan/allowed repair leaves zero complete documents
startup validates nonempty finished file without mutation
graphs.notes: Path for one file identity, not combinations with acknowledgment or owner lifetime. Durable here means surviving-process local filesystem fact, not fsync/host-crash durability. No finished-to-open transition. Rotation creates another identity. Automatic size/time rotation and local finished-file deletion are absent at HEAD. Recovery failures leave the relevant surviving paths for another open, with owner failure counted separately.

edges: first complete framed document reaches file
additional complete framed documents reach file
interrupted first document write leaves partial frame
interrupted later write leaves partial final frame
open-file recovery truncates UnexpectedEof tail with no preceding documents
open-file recovery truncates UnexpectedEof tail after complete documents
finished-file scan fails without repairing damage
recovery rejects malformed metadata, identity, magic or checksum without repair
recovery preserves complete records including records with no acknowledged success
empty finished file causes recovery error
graphs.notes: Content classification for a surviving open/finished file. File deletion and rename are in the path graph. UnexpectedEof repair applies only to document frames in open files with valid metadata. Corruption can be an initial scan condition. No speculative hardware-corruption transition is counted. An incomplete header in open is invalid, not repairable. Acknowledgment cannot be reconstructed from complete records.

edges: all framed documents flush to kernel and append returns file ID
failed-owner gate, empty/oversized input, metadata, arithmetic or logical-budget rejection
mutation or flush fails, leaving owner requiring recovery
graphs.notes: One synchronous caller's acknowledgment eligibility/result, not an async wait or function-stage graph. Success is the local API acknowledgment boundary. Actual HTTP delivery is unimplemented. A crash before return may leave complete unacknowledged records. Client retries can duplicate data. Failed appends can have partial effects. No fsync, S3 or search-visibility requirement on success.

edges: unchanged nonempty input uploaded under stable identity and upload established
failed or ambiguous upload retains local input for retry/reconciliation
metastore registration established for same input identity
failed or ambiguous registration retains local copy
recovery reconciles matching registered or completed identity
safe local deletion succeeds, releasing disk charge
local deletion fails and remains retryable
graphs.notes: Small ordered upload/register/delete protocol, expressed as established progress for the ingester. Local core implements only finished_local_retained. During a lost registration reply the metastore may already allow assignment even though the ingester has not advanced its knowledge. No product of those independent facts is counted. Keep local data on reconciliation failure. Registration retries must observe retained completion evidence. Exact object-key/content checks, response reconciliation and retry implementation remain open. Recovery mechanics are proposed within the selected handoff requirement. No handoff queue or serial worker is inferred.

edges: first conditional metastore transaction commits full output publication and input completion atomically
later publication observes already completed and preserves winner
repeated registration is discarded using retained completion evidence
graphs.notes: Two-state metastore fact. Metastore handles conditional atomicity and winner selection. All attempt outputs must be uploaded before publication. Assignment recency does not restrict publishing. No multi-party consensus, publish-lock lifecycle, leases, prepare/commit phases or separate client winner election. A lost response changes caller knowledge, not transaction atomicity. The same completion transaction applies to an empty output set. Schema/API/backend details are unimplemented.

edges: conditional metastore assignment records processing start while still eligible
competing conditional assignment loses and requester selects another file
unfinished processing start crosses retry threshold
another conditional assignment records new start
any attempt wins publication while recorded start is recent
any attempt wins publication after retry threshold
graphs.notes: Oldest-first candidate selection uses this gate. Registration initializes eligible_unstarted. Processing-start age is not task liveness. Expiry permits a new whole-file attempt without stopping or fencing the old one. No renewal or local assignment journal. Threshold, oldest-order timestamp and ambiguous assignment reply handling remain open. completed reuses the publication fact rather than adding a second counted completion state.

edges: attempt input read actually returns Pending
attempt output upload actually returns Pending
conditional publication request actually returns Pending
publication request completion or transport error wakes continuation
graphs.notes: One already-assigned attempt retains its continuation/resources across these genuine external dependencies. These are specified dependency classes, not observed ingesthree futures at HEAD. Immediate-ready calls need no dependency-state visit. Spurious wake/re-poll can re-enter the same pending state via shared runtime scheduling. Common ready/running scheduling, termination and OS blocking are supplied elsewhere. Parsing/indexing/serialization/packaging are not four scheduling states. Existing finalize is synchronous and process_indexed_split has no internal await. CPU/blocking offload, assignment polling, retries, merge-notification backpressure and executor/admission gates have no selected implementation and are not guessed.

edges: attempt constructs a split with selected RAM indexing mode
successful finalization persists output to disk and releases builder RAM
attempt releases finalized scratch output after use or termination
graphs.notes: Per split, not the cross-product for a many-split file. Same attempt owns both resource forms. Construction already has scratch-directory metadata. disk_output_owned denotes released construction RAM with retained finalized disk files. Serialization and packaging do not transfer ownership to another stage. Existing reusable RAM finalization supports this distinction, but ingesthree integration, failure cleanup and exact release timing remain unimplemented. Process death can leave filesystem debris. Resource release is not proof of crash-safe scratch deletion or immediate RSS reduction. This reusable resource-form distinction is also present on the current side; its current representation is spread across workbench, envelope custody and scratch-location graphs. Do not interpret raw inventory ratios as an equivalent-detail complexity percentage.

edges: some but not all outputs persist for multi-output attempt
all required outputs are available: one-output upload finishes, or the output set is empty after processing
additional outputs persist but complete set is still absent
last output persists, satisfying publication prerequisite
graphs.notes: Actual remote set for one attempt before cleanup, independent of result knowledge and resource lifetime. Successful PUT can persist despite a lost response. Partial upload matters because abandoned objects survive failure and cannot publish a full set. Full upload alone completes no input. Failure leaves the existing set. Subsequent object deletion is represented in cleanup rather than enumerating subsets. An empty output set satisfies the full-set prerequisite after processing completes. Output identity isolation and concrete upload concurrency remain unimplemented.

edges: successful transaction response or reconciliation establishes this attempt's published set
response or reconciliation establishes another attempt's published set
failure/lost reply leaves outcome unresolved for retry/reconciliation
graphs.notes: Caller knowledge for a submitted publication, separate from the two-state atomic metastore fact. No extra transaction stages. Do not delete this attempt's outputs merely because response was lost or an already-completed reply arrived: it may be the same attempt's prior success. Distinguishing own prior success from another winner is an explicitly unresolved API/evidence detail. NewSplits follows established success. Crash-gap rediscovery/notification delivery protocol is not specified and adds no invented states.

edges: atomic publication completes input with winner outputs published
delete succeeds or reconciliation establishes object already absent
delete fails or reply is unresolved and reconciliation retries
late redundant upload is found for an identity whose completion evidence remains
graphs.notes: Input deletion authorization after completion is selected. Periodic Janitor ownership is proposed and progress/late-upload mechanics are unimplemented. Reconciliation is completed input IDs intersect present input objects. Persisted completion evidence must remain so re-registration cannot recreate unfinished work. Deletion can proceed while a losing attempt runs. The late-upload edge records the documented cleanup obligation, not an implemented watcher or journal.

edges: establish object is unpublished and no still-allowed attempt can publish it
delete succeeds or reconciliation establishes absence
delete fails or reply is unresolved and reconciliation retries
late object is observed and the same no-publication safety condition still holds
graphs.notes: Per object authorization, not a GC subsystem. For a completed file, distinguish winner's set and delete only losing attempt objects. For an unfinished file, absent publication alone cannot authorize deletion while an old attempt or already-submitted transaction may still publish. Exact proof for abandoned work and ambiguous results is open. No lease, fence, age threshold, GC queue or consensus is selected. This graph captures the required guard and repeatable delete only.
